acceptance_criteria.criterion: generateWorkspaceFile() creates a valid JSON file with folders and settings when the file does not exist.
generateWorkspaceFile() preserves existing settings, extensions, and any other properties when the file already exists.
Each folder entry has the correct path (absolute) and name ("ProjectName (WORKSPACE_ID)") format.
removeWorkspaceFile() deletes the file and does not throw if the file is already absent.
getWorkspaceFilePath() returns the path in the format {projectsFolder}/{projectSlug}-{workspaceId}.code-workspace.

summary: Implemented src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts with three exported functions: getWorkspaceFilePath(), generateWorkspaceFile(), and removeWorkspaceFile(). generateWorkspaceFile() creates a new .code-workspace file with folders array and empty settings on first call, and on subsequent calls reads the existing file and replaces only the folders property while preserving all other properties (settings, extensions, custom keys). removeWorkspaceFile() silently no-ops when the file is absent. Added src/tests/vscode-workspace.test.ts with 13 tests covering all acceptance criteria. All 257 tests pass (13 new + 244 pre-existing).

comments.note: No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent. The module is simple, well-scoped, and follows existing project patterns (fs.mkdirSync recursive, JSON.stringify with 4-space indent + trailing newline).

summary: Reviewed src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts and src/tests/vscode-workspace.test.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info observation recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium | OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control / Path Traversal) | src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts — getWorkspaceFilePath() uses path.join(projectsFolder, `${projectSlug}-${workspaceId}.code-workspace`). While projectSlug is always sanitised through toKebabCase() ([a-z0-9-] only), workspaceId is passed in without sanitisation. If workspaceId were supplied as '../../../etc/passwd', path.join would resolve outside projectsFolder. In the current tool architecture workspaceId comes from user config and is effectively trusted, so the risk is Low-to-Medium in practice. Recommendation: add a guard (e.g. if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(workspaceId)) throw new Error('Invalid workspaceId')) inside getWorkspaceFilePath() so the function is self-defending.

Low | OWASP A05 (Security Misconfiguration) | src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts line ~72 — JSON parse exceptions in generateWorkspaceFile() are silently swallowed (catch block sets existing = null and recreates the file). Loss of an existing workspace file's settings could be surprising; at minimum, a warning-level log would aid diagnosis. Not a direct security risk but could mask unexpected file corruption.

Info | Defence-in-depth | src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts — generateWorkspaceFile() and removeWorkspaceFile() accept arbitrary filePath strings with no bounds check. Security correctness relies entirely on callers providing safe paths. This is acceptable for an internal library module but worth documenting via a JSDoc @throws or @param precondition note so future callers are aware.

summary: Reviewed src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts and src/tests/vscode-workspace.test.ts. Code is clean, well-scoped, and follows project conventions. All acceptance criteria met. No blocking issues found. Two minor observations recorded. PASS.

comments.note: generateWorkspaceFile() accepts repoPaths: { slug: string; path: string }[] but only uses repo.path — the slug field is never read. This is intentional per spec (all folders share the 'ProjectName (WORKSPACE_ID)' name), but the unused field in the parameter type may confuse future callers who expect slug to influence the output. Consider removing slug from the type or adding a comment explaining it is reserved for future use.

[documentation-forward] generateWorkspaceFile() JSDoc should clarify that all folder entries receive the same display name ('ProjectName (WORKSPACE_ID)') regardless of which repo they represent — the slug field in repoPaths is currently unused. Future contributors may expect per-repo name differentiation. Document the deliberate design choice.

notes: vscode-workspace.ts implements the three public functions the plan specifies. The generic WorkspaceFolder and VsCodeWorkspaceFile interfaces are module-private. The spread-merge pattern ({ ...existing, folders }) cleanly preserves all unknown properties. Tests cover: path format, new-file creation (with folders + empty settings), existing-file update (folders replaced, settings/extensions/custom keys preserved), parent-directory auto-creation, and removeWorkspaceFile no-throw on ENOENT.

Code is clean and ready for documentation. Note the two open items: (1) unused slug field in repoPaths — document as deliberate design choice; (2) silent JSON parse swallow in generateWorkspaceFile — comment explains intent but worth surfacing in docs.
